base: T3_rev6 row 38 / N2, E_a0_conv=1.90 -- identical to the T13 lnl=0 rows so the ONLY change is the channel
rationale: T13 showed the <100> cost is NOT the size obstacle: lowering it via n_ref moved the answer by 1e-9 because dF gates only Gamma_uni while <100> forms kinetically.  What T13 DID show is that loop growth is unbounded -- 3.3-3.9 nm at 0.5 dpa but 21.9 nm and pile_100 = 0.94-0.99 by 6.5 dpa -- so the loops pass THROUGH the measured 10-15 nm band and run to the grid ceiling.  Nothing caps them.  LOOP_NETWORK_LOSS is the channel designed to do exactly that (CLAUDE.md objective (a), saturate loop density), and it has been off for every calibration run since it measured inert -- but that was at ION conditions where Lambda_net*t ~ 1e-3.  At neutron dose the same estimate gives ~20.  chi must be high or P_ld is identically zero (chi=1 gives Lambda_net == 0 at every size), hence 30 and 60.
